# Third-party notices: Win For All for Android

**This file is a licence condition, not documentation.** Every component listed below is conveyed to the user inside the installed APK, and every licence below requires its notice to accompany that distribution. A build that ships the binaries and not this file is out of compliance.

Generated by `platform/android/licence_conveyance/generate_notices.py` from a frozen inventory. Do not hand-edit: the next run overwrites it and `ThirdPartyNoticesConveyanceTest` fails on drift. To change it, change the dependency or `resolutions.json` and regenerate.

## What is covered

| Layer | Components | Where it is conveyed |
|---|---:|---|
| Android/JVM libraries | 169 | `classes*.dex`, merged resources |
| Rust crates | 244 | `lib/*/libwins_api.so`, `lib/*/libwins_jni_android.so` |
| YARA rule corpora | 3 | rule text compiled into both `.so` files |
| Bundled font | 1 | `assets/flutter_assets/fonts/` |
| Bundled BlazePose models | 2 | `assets/posture_pose/*.tflite` (section 10) |
| Flutter engine and Dart packages | 182 | `lib/*/libflutter.so`; notices in `assets/flutter_assets/NOTICES.Z` |

ABIs covered: aarch64-linux-android, x86_64-linux-android.

## UNRESOLVED: read this first

The following conveyed components could **not** be given a correct notice. They are named rather than papered over. Each is a release blocker in its own right.

| Component | Declared licence | Why it is unresolved |
|---|---|---|
| `ascii_tree 0.1.1` | MIT | STILL UNRESOLVED AFTER AN UPSTREAM ATTEMPT ON 2026-08-08, and it is now believed unresolvable. Two independent failures, either of which alone is fatal. (1) NO TIE: the published .crate contains no .cargo_vcs_info.json -- it was published in 2018, before cargo emitted that file -- so there is no way to establish which commit produced 0.1.1. (2) NO UPSTREAM: the repository its manifest names, github.com/bpressure/ascii_tree, returns 404. It is gone, so there is nothing to fetch from even without a tie. The crate is 1,781 bytes and contains exactly four files (Cargo.toml.orig, Cargo.toml, README.md, src/lib.rs); its own `include` list is [".gitignore", "Cargo.toml", "src/*.rs", "README.md"], which would have excluded a LICENSE even if one had existed upstream. The only other release, 0.1.0 (2017), also ships no licence file. The sole identity published anywhere is the manifest `authors` field, an e-mail address -- an author is not a copyright line, and writing one from it would be inventing the notice. |
| `tinyzip 0.4.0` | MIT | STILL UNRESOLVED AFTER AN UPSTREAM ATTEMPT ON 2026-08-08, but for the OPPOSITE reason to ascii_tree, and the distinction matters. The tie here is PERFECT: .cargo_vcs_info.json names git sha1 26cdbc441d5db08ac26bfbd7ba23557707d8524a, that commit exists in github.com/lovasoa/tinyzip, and of the 254 file paths present in both the .crate and the repository at that commit, ZERO differ in content and there are ZERO crate-only files. So we know exactly which tree produced this release. THE PROBLEM IS THAT THE TREE HAS NO LICENCE TEXT IN IT. There is no LICENSE, COPYING or NOTICE file anywhere in the entire repository at that commit -- not at the root, not in any subdirectory -- and none at the default branch today either. GitHub reports the repository's license field as null. The README contains no copyright or licence section. No licence file appears in any of the four published releases (0.1.0 through 0.4.0). The manifest declares license = "MIT" and has no `authors` field at all. So the MIT GRANT is declared and we rely on it, but the MIT NOTICE that clause requires to be reproduced -- 'the above copyright notice' -- has never been published by the copyright holder in any artifact or any tree. It cannot be fetched because it does not exist. Composing one from the GitHub account name would be inventing the notice, which this project refuses. |

## 3. YARA detection-rule corpora

Reproduced from `core/yara_engine/rules/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, which the detection-content lane generated from the hash-pinned upstream commits on 2026-08-08. It carries the three upstream licence texts in full.

**The author lists below are not the ones in that file.** The tool that wrote them capped each list at 200 entries and then declared the count *after* the cap, so the DRL-1.1 list stated "200 distinct rule authors require attribution" above 200 names while 277 require it: an undercount that rewrote its own header, and therefore invisible to any check that compared the file only to itself. DRL-1.1's sharing conditions require author identification to travel with the rules, and this file ships inside the APK, so the truncation was a live conveyance gap on the licence covering 5,309 of the 6,691 vendored rules. The cap is removed and the complete lists: 299 identifications across the three corpora: are reproduced here, re-derived from the vendored rule text that actually ships by `platform/android/licence_conveyance/derive_rule_attribution.py` and frozen in `rule_attribution.json`. No identification present in the earlier lists was removed.

==============================================================================
# Third-party rule notices: conveyance obligations

**This file is not documentation. It is a licence condition.**

Every rule set vendored into `core/yara_engine/rules/` is under a licence that
requires attribution to travel with redistribution. The Win For All app
redistributes these rules inside its binary, so **any build that ships
`wins_yara_engine` must also ship the notices below in a place the user can
reach.** A build that ships the rules and not the notices is out of compliance
with DRL-1.1 and with MIT, both of which require the notice to accompany
"copies or substantial portions".

An audit on 2026-08-08 found the Android build ships **zero** licence files
today. That is a pre-existing gap, it is a store blocker on its own, and this
pack adds three more obligations to it. Closing it is a `platform/android`
task; this lane's territory is `core/` and it could not close it here.

## What must be reproduced

| Source | Licence | Obligation |
|---|---|---|
| `Neo23x0/signature-base` | Detection Rule License 1.1 | Retain author identification for every rule. Commercial redistribution is explicitly permitted. |
| `reversinglabs/reversinglabs-yara-rules` | MIT | Reproduce the copyright notice and permission notice. |
| `bartblaze/Yara-rules` | MIT | Reproduce the copyright notice and permission notice. |

The first row is the repository default, not the whole story. 127 rules inside
`signature-base` are third-party contributions carrying their own licence,
stated in a comment at the head of the file rather than in any rule's `meta`,
and until 2026-08-09 every one of them was attributed here as DRL-1.1. They
are not DRL-1.1, and each brings an attribution obligation of its own:

| Rules | Licence | Rights holder | Obligation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 90 | Apache-2.0 | Google LLC (GCTI Cobalt Strike, Sliver) | §4(a) supply the licence text: satisfied by this project's own `LICENSE`, which is Apache-2.0; §4(c) retain the notices in the rule text: the file-header comment is carried verbatim in `signature_base.yar`; §4(d) reproduce attribution notices. |
| 14 | BSD-2-Clause | FireEye, Inc. / Mandiant | Reproduce the copyright notice and the conditions in the documentation or other materials. |
| 9 | MIT | nao_sec | Reproduce the copyright notice and permission notice. |
| 5 | BSD-3-Clause variant | JPCERT Coordination Center | Reproduce the copyright notice and conditions. Additionally: no derived product may carry the JPCERT/CC name or use it as endorsement. This product does neither. |
| 8 | BSD-2-Clause | Volexity, Inc. | As above. |
| 1 | BSD-2-Clause | ditekSHen | As above. |

The per-rule author lists that satisfy all of the above are reproduced
verbatim below, generated by `tools/rule_pack/apply_license_policy.py` from
each rule's own `meta.author` field, bucketed by the licence actually in force
for that rule rather than by the repository default.

## What was deliberately NOT taken, and why

* **`elastic/protections-artifacts` (Elastic License v2)**: source-available,
  not OSI-approved. `tools/rule_pack/license_policy.json` classifies ELv2
  `client_pack_allowed: false` as a conservative default, and says to flip it
  only on an explicit recorded decision. No such decision exists, so 2,876
  rules were fetched, verified, measured: and not shipped.
* **`Yara-Rules/rules` (GPL-2.0)**: rejected twice over. The copyleft question
  for rule data shipped beside a proprietary binary is unresolved, AND the set
  flags 100.00% of macOS system binaries. Either alone disqualifies it.
* **`avast/ioc`**: no LICENSE file at the repository root, so all rights are
  reserved and nothing may be redistributed.
* **ClamAV CVD**: GPL-2.0 with no separate signature-database redistribution
  grant published by Talos.
* **abuse.ch MalwareBazaar**: the published FAQ gates commercial use behind a
  paid subscription.

## Rules removed for licence reasons before vendoring

71 rules from `signature-base` are stripped rule-by-rule before vendoring. The
full list, with each rule's declared licence string and which surface it was
declared on, is in
`tools/rule_pack/receipts/license/signature_base__excluded_rules.json`.

**24 found by reading each rule's own `meta: license =`** (2026-08-08): 13
under CC BY-NC 4.0 and 11 pointing at a third party's LICENSE file without
naming a licence. It was 30 until 2026-08-09; see "A pointer answered inside
the artifact" below.

**47 more found by reading file-header comments** (2026-08-09). The licence
filter had only ever read per-rule `meta`, and these rules declare their
licence in a block comment above the rules instead. 27 of the 47 were in the
shipped pack: the other 20 had already been dropped for needing a YARA
external variable the engine cannot define:

| Rules shipping | Licence | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 11 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | `yara/apt_apt41.yar` |
| 7 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | `yara/crime_nansh0u.yar` |
| 3 | CC BY-NC 4.0 | `yara/crime_xbash.yar` |
| 5 | unresolved pointer to SigmaHQ's LICENSE file | `yara/apt_greyenergy.yar` |
| 1 | GPL (unversioned) | `yara/gen_loaders.yar`: `ReflectiveLoader` |

## A pointer answered inside the artifact

Six rules moved the other way on 2026-08-09, from excluded to shipping, and the
reason is worth stating precisely because "we decided a rejected licence was
fine after all" is the shape of a mistake.

They are `APT_MAL_Win_BlueLight` and `APT_MAL_Win_BlueLight_B` in
`yara/apt_apt37_bluelight.yar`, and `APT_RUBY_RokRat_Loader`,
`APT_PY_BlueLight_Loader`, `APT_MAL_Win_DecRok` and
`APT_MAL_Win_RokLoad_Loader` in `yara/apt_nk_inkysquid.yar`. Each carries

    license = "See license at https://github.com/volexity/threat-intel/LICENSE.txt"

which names no licence, so the policy classified it
`THIRD-PARTY-REFERENCE-REQUIRES-REVIEW` and refused to ship it. That was the
right default for a pointer nobody had followed.

**Both files reproduce the licence they point at, in full, above the rules**: 
`Copyright 2021 by Volexity, Inc.`, `The 2-Clause BSD License`, the source-form
and binary-form conditions, and the whole AS IS disclaimer. That header is
carried verbatim in `signature_base.yar` and ships inside the APK. The meta says
*see the licence at this URL*; the file hands the reader that licence. Nothing
was unresolved.

**This is not a precedent that a header resolves a pointer.** Another vendor's
URL might target a document whose contents differ from whatever header they
happen to ship, and the artifact would not reveal the difference. So the
resolution is declared for one rights holder, in
`tools/rule_pack/license_policy.json` under
`licence_declaration_surfaces.pointer_resolution`, keyed on *both* the pointer
and the required header text. The negative control is in this same corpus:
`yara/apt_sharptongue.yar` carries the same Volexity pointer, has no licence
header at all, matches the pointer, fails the header: and remains excluded.

Volexity's rules are attributed under BSD-2-Clause below. Before restoring them
they were measured for false positives, because a settled licence question does
not make a noisy rule shippable: 0 matches over 155,184 benign files across six
corpora, with a synthetic positive control confirming the rules can fire at all.
Receipts are in `tools/rule_pack/receipts/fp_sweeps/`.

The 21 CC BY-NC rules are the reason this matters rather than being tidiness.
NonCommercial forbids commercial use, this product is commercial, and
NonCommercial is non-free under the OSI, FSF and DFSG definitions alike. They
were shipping. They are not any more, and the filter that missed them now
reads both surfaces, so a rule-pack update cannot re-admit them.

The Rust PE header reader includes compatibility code for pefile 2024.8.26. This supplemental notice accompanies that code; it does not establish complete PE extraction or model readiness.

Covers `pefile 2024.8.26 header compatibility`.

Source: `core/ai_engine/src/ember/pe/mod.rs`.

of pefile 2024.8.26. The upstream source is available at

byte sequences and records numeric output from that pinned local oracle.

## 9. NULLSET-2 overwrite engine (vendored C core)

The Safe Deletion feature's multi-pass overwrite engine is the NULLSET-2 reference core (pure C11), vendored as the first-party crate `core/nullset_vendor` at upstream v4.3.1, head `fb8d9ab`, and compiled into `libwins_api.so` for both shipped ABIs. Because the carrying crate is first-party, the crate inventory cannot see this obligation; it is pinned here.

Covers `nullset_vendor 4.3.1` (vendored C sources, both ABIs).

Dual licence **AGPL-3.0-only OR Commercial**; this embedding is conveyed under the copyright holder's own commercial track.

## 10. Posture View: LiteRT runtime and bundled BlazePose models

Posture View runs the bundled detector and landmark models through the bare LiteRT (TensorFlow Lite) interpreter. The runtime and weights have separate licence entries below; this path does not bundle the MediaPipe Tasks SDK.
